title: Northern War (Flagstaff War)
summary: On 11 March 1845 Hōne Heke, Kawiti and their warriors attacked Kororāreka, felled the flagstaff on Maiki Hill, and the town was left in ruins. The colonial government ordered a full-scale offensive. British troops advanced on Ruapekapeka pā in December 1845 and captured it, though many consider the battle a draw.

uncertainty.note: Start is the dated attack on Kororāreka (11 March 1845). The opened pages place the advance on Ruapekapeka in early December 1845; the end of the war is not dated on them, so the end year is set to 1845.

as_recorded.value: At sunset on 11 March 1845, the town was a smouldering ruin.
began to advance on Ruapekapeka in early December 1845

where.historical_name: Kororāreka, Bay of Islands, New Zealand

importance.justification: Large-scale fighting between Māori forces and the colonial government in the north of New Zealand.

reviewer_note: Least sure of the end date: the opened pages do not date the peace, so the record ends 1845 although the war is usually dated into early 1846 in sources not opened here. Pin is Kororāreka; Ruapekapeka lies inland. Tohu Whenua is a Heritage New Zealand and Department of Conservation programme (not confirmed on the page).
